predictions.headline: Nashville to score twice at Boston, even against the Bruins' stingy defence
predictions.body: Nashville are 3-2-3 through eight games and have scored 23 goals in that span, but the reason this line is attractive is shot volume rather than finishing: Filip Forsberg has put 24 shots on goal in eight games for a single goal, and Steven Stamkos has 14 shots and 10 points from the same span. Boston have conceded only 22 goals in ten games, one of the best rates in the league, which is exactly why the team total sits at 1.5 rather than 2.5. Two goals is the realistic floor for a club generating this much rubber, and the model puts it at 71.1%, one of only four selections on the slate that clears the brief's rule.
facts: 22 goals against in 8 games (2.75 per game)
4 goals, 6 assists, 10 points, 14 shots, 2 power-play goals

predictions.headline: Utah to stay within one goal in Seattle
predictions.body: Utah have won seven of ten and scored 38 goals, and the offence runs through two players who are both above a point a game: Nick Schmaltz has seven goals and six assists with five of those goals on the power play, and Clayton Keller has four and nine. Seattle have scored almost as much, 37 goals in ten, but have conceded 34 and have already lost three times, so a one-goal Seattle win still cashes this line. The model gives Utah a 70.5% chance of not losing by two or more, which makes it the thinnest of the three Highs and the one most exposed if Utah's 36.1% power play turns out to be a five-game artefact.
facts: 7 goals, 6 assists, 13 points, 5 power-play goals, 31 shots

predictions.headline: San Jose to score twice in Ottawa
predictions.body: San Jose are 5-4-1 with 26 goals in ten games, and the scoring is unusually concentrated: Macklin Celebrini has 14 points in eight games from 37 shots, including an overtime winner, while Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg have seven points each. Ottawa are 7-3-0 and have conceded 24 goals in ten, so the Senators are the tougher half of this matchup and the total sits low for that reason. The model still gives the Sharks a 70.4% chance of two goals or more, because a team putting up Celebrini's shot volume usually gets there, and the same shape of bet as the Nashville line is the one this desk is most comfortable repeating.
facts: 5 goals, 9 assists, 14 points, 37 shots in 8 games

predictions.headline: Under 7.5 goals between two clubs that are not converting their chances
predictions.body: New Jersey's nine games have produced 59 goals and Anaheim's 55, and neither side is finishing at a rate that suggests a burst: Jack Hughes has nine points but only two goals from 35 shots, and Leo Carlsson's eleven points have come from just eleven shots, a conversion rate no player sustains. Both clubs are conceding around three goals a game — 30 in nine for the Devils, 29 in nine for the Ducks — so the model's expected total lands close to six. Under 7.5 clears the 70% test at 70.0% and a fair price of −234, which is the fourth and last selection inside the brief's window.
facts: 2 goals, 7 assists, 9 points, 35 shots, 2 overtime goals

findings.title: The High gate can only ever return a 1.43-point band of probabilities
findings.detail: More than 70% implies a fair American price shorter than −233.33. Requiring that price to be no shorter than −250 leaves 70.00% < p ≤ 71.43%. The +10000 end of the stated range corresponds to 0.99% and is unreachable in a two-way market. The rule therefore selects on price proximity, not on confidence.
findings.impact: Every High on this desk. Needs a decision from whoever wrote the brief.

findings.title: One in-band EuroLeague selection is capped at Medium for lack of player evidence
findings.detail: Anadolu Efes v Besiktas over 166.5 points prices at 71.2% (−247) and passes both tests in the brief's rule. No official EuroLeague player-level source was available to this session, so the required write-up could not be produced. The price is published; the tier is Medium. It is now the only in-band selection on the desk that is not published as High.
findings.impact: One selection. Visible on the markets page with its price intact.

findings.title: The strongest line on the slate is excluded by the price floor
findings.detail: Panathinaikos at home to Baskonia prices at 81.8% with a fair price of −451. It clears the probability test by twelve points and fails the −250 test by two hundred. The same is true of 167 other selections above 70%.
findings.impact: The desk's best information is published as Medium, not High.

findings.title: EuroLeague tip-off times are inherited, not re-read
findings.detail: The standings feed used for ratings publishes results only. Tip-off times come from the 07:17Z canonical observation of the round 7 game centre, five hours before this desk was built, and are marked as inherited on every EuroLeague fixture.
findings.impact: Nine fixtures. A schedule change after 07:17Z would not be reflected.

findings.title: No game-level recent results were read
findings.detail: The club schedule feeds return the full season and were too large to read within this session's budget. Form is therefore expressed as season-to-date record, goals for, goals against and per-player scoring totals, not as a list of recent scorelines.
findings.impact: All three predictions. The brief asked for recent match history; this is a partial answer.

findings.title: Fourteen of seventeen in-scope categories have no verified input
findings.detail: Only ice hockey, basketball and baseball produced fixtures that could be re-read from an official feed in this window. The other fourteen categories are kept as empty pages rather than filled with remembered fixtures from earlier windows.
findings.impact: Coverage. The gap is structural, not an oversight.

findings.title: NHL venues were visible for only five of twelve games
findings.detail: The schedule feed returns venue inside each game object; the read covered games 154 to 158. The remaining seven venues are blank rather than reconstructed from general knowledge.
findings.impact: Seven fixture rows on the matches page.

findings.title: MLB pricing rests on two clubs' rates, not a league run environment
findings.detail: Run expectations are the mean of each batting side's runs scored and each bowling side's runs allowed per game, with a fixed home adjustment. No league-average run environment was read, so totals and run lines are labelled as model output and the desk does not claim they match a market.
findings.impact: Two priced World Series games. Game 2 also has no announced starter.

findings.title: The models are uncalibrated and the sensitivity ranges are wider than the gate
findings.detail: None of the priced fixtures had started when the desk was built, so no outcome backtest exists. Re-running each High across the shrinkage and home-advantage grid moves it by three to five percentage points, which is two to three times the width of the 70.00–71.43% window.
findings.impact: Every probability on the desk. Treat tiers as labels, not guarantees.

findings.title: The EuroLeague model was recalibrated by judgement, and that is disclosed
findings.detail: A multiplicative attack/defence model priced Panathinaikos at 97.5% for this fixture, which no basketball market would sustain. The published version shrinks each club's points differential toward zero and applies half of the remaining gap, which moves that match to 81.8%. The 0.50 weight is a judgement call, chosen so the largest favourite on the slate lands near 82%.
